11-19.name: Las Vegas Grand Prix
11-19.fact: Max Verstappen won despite a five-second penalty as Charles Leclerc took second on the final lap.

03-02.name: Bahrain Grand Prix
03-02.fact: Max Verstappen took pole, the win, fastest lap and led every lap for his fifth grand chelem.

12-08.name: Abu Dhabi Grand Prix
12-08.fact: Lando Norris won from pole to clinch McLaren's first constructors' title in 26 years.

11-30.name: Qatar Grand Prix
11-30.fact: Max Verstappen pounced on a McLaren safety-car blunder to win and force a three-way title decider.

12-07.name: Abu Dhabi Grand Prix
12-07.fact: Max Verstappen won the race, but Lando Norris's third place sealed his first title by two points.

01-03.name: Michael Schumacher born
01-03.fact: Michael Schumacher was born in Hürth, West Germany, and grew up to win seven world titles.

01-04.name: Donald Campbell's final run
01-04.fact: Donald Campbell died on Coniston Water at 328 mph, chasing one more water speed record.

01-05.name: Dakar Rally reaches Saudi Arabia
01-05.fact: The Dakar Rally rolled out of Jeddah, opening its first edition in Saudi Arabia and in Asia.

01-06.name: Targa Florio founder dies
01-06.fact: Vincenzo Florio, the Sicilian who invented the Targa Florio road race in 1906, died at 75.

01-07.name: Lewis Hamilton born
01-07.fact: Lewis Hamilton was born in Stevenage; he would go on to win more Grands Prix than anyone.

01-08.name: Vanderbilt Cup founder dies
01-08.fact: William Kissam Vanderbilt II died; his Vanderbilt Cup gave America its first great road race.

01-10.name: Rory Byrne born
01-10.fact: Rory Byrne is born; his Benetton and Ferrari designs won Michael Schumacher all seven of his titles.

01-11.name: Carroll Shelby born
01-11.fact: Carroll Shelby is born in Texas: a Le Mans winner who built the Cobra and Ford's Ferrari-beating GT40.

01-14.name: Dan Gurney dies
01-14.fact: Dan Gurney dies at 86, the man who won a Grand Prix in his own Eagle and began the champagne shower.

01-20.name: Sid Watkins retires
01-20.fact: Sid Watkins steps down as F1's medical chief after 26 years of pulling drivers from wrecks.

01-24.name: 24 Hours of Daytona
01-24.fact: David Donohue holds off Juan Pablo Montoya by 0.167s, the closest finish in Daytona 24 history.

01-30.name: Ferdinand Porsche dies
01-30.fact: Ferdinand Porsche dies in Stuttgart, leaving behind the Beetle, the Silver Arrows and a racing dynasty.

01-31.name: 24 Hours of Daytona
01-31.fact: Martin Brundle's Jaguar XJR-9 won Daytona by one lap, ending eleven straight Porsche-powered wins.

02-01.name: 24 Hours of Daytona
02-01.fact: Porsche's new 917K won its Daytona debut by 45 laps, with Pedro Rodríguez leading the charge.

02-02.name: Roger Williamson born
02-02.fact: Roger Williamson was born; his 1973 death at Zandvoort and David Purley's lone rescue bid shook F1.

02-03.name: 24 Hours of Daytona
02-03.fact: A.J. Foyt won the Daytona 24 again, the only man to also take Indy, Le Mans and the Daytona 500.

02-05.name: Land speed record at Daytona
02-05.fact: Malcolm Campbell hurled Blue Bird to 246 mph on Daytona Beach and was knighted weeks later.

02-06.name: Robert Kubica's rally crash
02-06.fact: A rally crash nearly tore off Robert Kubica's right arm; he fought back to F1 eight years later.

02-08.name: Williams founded
02-08.fact: Frank Williams and Patrick Head founded Williams Grand Prix Engineering; nine constructors' titles followed.

02-09.name: Le Mans founder dies
02-09.fact: Charles Faroux, who helped invent the 24 Hours of Le Mans and ran it from 1923 to 1956, died at 84.

02-10.name: First Ferrari driver born
02-10.fact: Franco Cortese was born: he drove the very first Ferrari and handed the marque its first win.

02-12.name: New York to Paris Race
02-12.fact: Six cars left New York's Times Square for Paris, and 169 days later the Thomas Flyer won.

02-13.name: Team Lotus wound up
02-13.fact: A court wound up Team Lotus for good: seven constructors' titles, from Jim Clark to Ayrton Senna.

02-14.name: Ronnie Peterson born
02-14.fact: Ronnie Peterson, the Superswede who won 10 Grands Prix but never a title, was born in Örebro.

02-15.name: Graham Hill born
02-15.fact: Graham Hill was born — still the only driver to win Monaco, the Indy 500 and Le Mans.

02-16.name: Jean Behra born
02-16.fact: Jean Behra was born — the French charger who lost an ear in a crash and kept racing anyway.

02-17.name: Fastest Daytona 500
02-17.fact: Buddy Baker averaged 177.6 mph to win the Daytona 500 — no one has run it faster since.

02-18.name: Enzo Ferrari born
02-18.fact: Enzo Ferrari was born in Modena; the Scuderia he founded in 1929 still races in Formula 1.

02-19.name: Blue Bird land speed record
02-19.fact: Malcolm Campbell blasted his Blue Bird to 206 mph on Daytona's sand for the land speed record.

02-20.name: Roger Penske born
02-20.fact: Roger Penske was born — his teams went on to win the Indianapolis 500 a record 20 times.

02-21.name: NASCAR founded
02-21.fact: Bill France Sr. put his name to NASCAR's founding papers, and stock car racing finally had one rulebook.

02-22.name: Niki Lauda born
02-22.fact: Niki Lauda was born in Vienna — the man who would survive fire at the Nürburgring and win two more titles.

02-23.name: Juan Manuel Fangio kidnapped
02-23.fact: Juan Manuel Fangio was seized at gunpoint in his Havana hotel by Cuban rebels who wanted the race stopped.

02-24.name: Alain Prost born
02-24.fact: Alain Prost was born in Lorette, France, and grew into four world titles won on brains, not bravado.

02-25.name: Jean Todt born
02-25.fact: Jean Todt was born in Pierrefort, the future boss who rebuilt Ferrari into Michael Schumacher's dynasty.

02-26.name: Daytona 500
02-26.fact: Mario Andretti won the Daytona 500 — still the only driver born outside the United States to do it.

02-27.name: Daytona 500 under the lights
02-27.fact: Rain pushed the Daytona 500 to Monday night, where Juan Pablo Montoya's crash set a jet dryer ablaze.

02-28.name: Mario Andretti born
02-28.fact: Mario Andretti was born in Istria; ahead of him lay the Daytona 500, the Indy 500 and an F1 title.

02-29.name: Masten Gregory born
02-29.fact: Masten Gregory was born on leap day; in 1965 he won Le Mans in the last Ferrari to do so for 58 years.

08-20.name: 1939 Swiss Grand Prix
08-20.fact: Hermann Lang won at Bremgarten for Mercedes — no German would win in a German car again until 2012.

11-10.name: Lucien Bianchi born
11-10.fact: Lucien Bianchi was born; he won Le Mans in 1968 and died testing at the same track six months later.

11-16.name: Tazio Nuvolari born
11-16.fact: Tazio Nuvolari was born; in 1935 he beat the mighty Silver Arrows at the Nürburgring in an old Alfa.

11-22.name: Robert Kubica's F1 return
11-22.fact: Williams signed Robert Kubica for 2019, almost eight years after a rally crash nearly took his arm.

11-28.name: Chicago Times-Herald race
11-28.fact: Frank Duryea won America's first automobile race, taking over ten hours to cover 54 miles.

12-02.name: John Cobb born
12-02.fact: John Cobb was born; in 1947 one Bonneville run hit 403 mph — first past 400, though his record averaged 394.

12-03.name: Bobby Allison born
12-03.fact: Bobby Allison was born; in 1988 he won the Daytona 500 with son Davey Allison right behind him.

12-04.name: Felice Nazzaro born
12-04.fact: Felice Nazzaro was born; in 1907 his Fiat won the Targa Florio, Kaiserpreis and French Grand Prix.

12-09.name: Al Unser dies
12-09.fact: Al Unser died at 82; he won the Indianapolis 500 four times, the last at 47 as its oldest winner.

12-10.name: Audi R18 unveiled
12-10.fact: Audi revealed the R18 in Ingolstadt; its hybrid version became the first electrified Le Mans winner.

12-11.name: Denis Jenkinson born
12-11.fact: Denis Jenkinson was born; his roller-map pace notes carried Stirling Moss to the 1955 Mille Miglia win.

12-14.name: NASCAR's founding meeting
12-14.fact: Bill France Sr. opened the Daytona Beach hotel meeting that would give birth to NASCAR.

12-15.name: Clay Regazzoni dies
12-15.fact: Clay Regazzoni, who gave Williams its first Grand Prix win, died in a motorway crash at 67.

12-16.name: Colin Chapman dies
12-16.fact: Colin Chapman, the Lotus founder who brought ground effect to F1, died of a heart attack at 54.

12-17.name: Budweiser Rocket run
12-17.fact: Stan Barrett's rocket car hit a claimed 739 mph, the first car said to break the sound barrier.

12-18.name: First land speed record
12-18.fact: Gaston de Chasseloup-Laubat set the first official land speed record, 63 km/h, in an electric Jeantaud.

12-19.name: Ralph DePalma born
12-19.fact: Ralph DePalma was born, the man who pushed his broken Mercedes to the line at Indy in 1912.

12-20.name: Karl Wendlinger born
12-20.fact: Karl Wendlinger was born; the 1994 Monaco crash left him in a coma for weeks, and he came back.

12-21.name: Lorenzo Bandini born
12-21.fact: Lorenzo Bandini was born, the Ferrari man who won Le Mans in 1963 and died at Monaco in 1967.

12-22.name: Pierre Levegh born
12-22.fact: Pierre Levegh was born; in 1952 he drove Le Mans alone and led by four laps until his engine broke.

12-23.name: Michael Schumacher returns
12-23.fact: Seven-time champion Michael Schumacher joined Mercedes, ending three years away from Formula 1.

12-24.name: John Cooper dies
12-24.fact: John Cooper, who put the engine behind the driver and rewrote Formula 1, died aged 77.

12-25.name: Louis Chevrolet born
12-25.fact: Louis Chevrolet, the racing driver whose name ended up on millions of cars, was born.

12-26.name: Adrian Newey born
12-26.fact: Adrian Newey was born; his cars would later win 14 drivers' titles for Williams, McLaren and Red Bull.

12-27.name: Jean Rondeau dies
12-27.fact: Jean Rondeau, the only man to win Le Mans in a car bearing his own name, was killed by a train.

12-30.name: Karel Loprais dies
12-30.fact: Karel Loprais, the Tatra truck ace they called Monsieur Dakar for his six wins, died at 72.

12-31.name: Malcolm Campbell dies
12-31.fact: Malcolm Campbell, the first man to drive a car past 300 mph, died with nine land speed records.
